page.layout: One page of text in a single column, with a verse passage set in italic lines below the prose. Margin notes in the right margin: "NB.", "Duo lu-", "scinia fer-", "monem", "humanu", "imitantes", "Ratisbo-", "na." Running head at top: PROROGANDA A. with page number 381 at top right.

main_text.p: tereaq; meditantes in diem, & assiduè noua loquentes longiori etiam contextu. Docentur autem secreto, & vbi nulla alia vox misceatur, assidente qui crebrò dicat ea quæ cōdita velit, ac cibis blandiente. Memorabile NB. est & admirabile, de lusciniis duabus hominum sermones imitatis Ratisbonæ in Comitiis, an. 1546. de quibus Gesnerus ipse sic scribit : Ego profecto nunquam Plinio nostro credidissem, multa adeo miranda de auicula hac scribenti, nisi ipse has bestiolas talia promentes & oculis vidissem, & auribus hisce audiuissem. Hæc Gesnerus. Placuit hoc reponere in gratiam Lectoris Carmen T. Vespasiani Strozæ in philomelam, lib. 6. Erotien:

p.i: Quæ virides umbras & loca sacra tenes.

l.i: Mollibus & variis quæ tot discrimina vocum,
Munere protali tibi quid philomela rependam?
Premia quæ tanto digna labore putem?
Dum vagus huc illuc hortis genialibus erro,
Hospitio officio tu protinus, usa benigni,
Fingis in aduentu carmina mille meo,
Nec procul hinc densis canis abdita frodib°, alta
Verùs hic Iuniperi infidis mihi proxima trunco,

page.notes: Right margin notes are a fragment of a heading "Duo lusciniae sermones imitantes humanos Ratisbonae" split across lines; reproduced as printed. Marginal "NB." and short fragments kept as printed. "Ratisbo-" and "na." are the last line of that margin note. Doubtful: "Et" at the foot of the verse, "frodib°" and "Hospitio" (printed "Hospitij"/"Hospitiù"), "venerata" (possibly printed with a Cyrillic-looking a, rendered as Latin a). Lines of verse set in italic. Word "Quæ" at line-start has a superscript mark. Some letters in the scan are faint and uncertain; treat the verse readings with caution.
